Why Does the Portal Say "File Size Too Large" After I Compressed My Photo?

By Kamlesh Mohabe, Software Engineer · Published 2026-10-04

Reasons a form still rejects an image after compression: 1KB definitions, hidden minimums, wrong format, renamed files, and how to fix each one.

Question: My file is 20 KB but the form says it is too large. Why?

The most common cause is how kilobytes are counted. This site counts 1 KB as 1,024 bytes. Some operating systems and some portals count 1 KB as 1,000 bytes. A file shown as 20.0 KB under one rule can exceed 20 KB under the other. The practical fix is to leave a margin: aim for 18 or 19 KB when the limit is 20 KB.

Question: Could the file be too small instead?

Yes. Many portals set a minimum as well as a maximum. A simple signature on white paper can compress to just a few KB, and then the portal says the file is invalid. If your range is 10–20 KB and the result is 6 KB, use a larger or sharper original, crop less tightly, or keep more of the surrounding paper.

Question: Does the file format matter, or just the extension?

It matters. Some portals check the real contents, not just the name. A PNG that was renamed to .jpg is still a PNG. To get a genuine JPEG, use JPEG output in the tool, and check that the downloaded file ends in .jpg. ImageTo20KB never labels a file as JPEG unless it was encoded as one.

Question: The size is right but the form still complains about dimensions.

Some forms check pixel width and height as well. This tool preserves your aspect ratio and only reduces dimensions, so crop to the correct shape first and set a maximum width in Advanced settings. Check the dimensions on the result card against the notice.

Question: The upload fails with a vague error.

Try a different browser, turn off extensions that interfere with uploads, check your internet connection, and avoid special characters or very long names in the file name. If the file is within range and in the right format, the error may be temporary on the portal side. Wait and try again later.

Question: Could I be using old numbers?

Very often. Size limits change between recruitment cycles. A figure from last year’s forum post may not apply. Treat the instructions on the portal as the source of truth, and treat any website’s numbers, including ours, as a guide to confirm.

A short troubleshooting list

Check the range printed on the upload screen. Aim a few KB under the maximum. Make sure you are above the minimum. Confirm it is a real JPEG. Match the dimensions if they are given. Rename the file only if the instructions require it. Keep your original in case you need to start again.

When to contact the portal helpdesk

If the file is in the right format, within the stated range, with the right dimensions, and it still fails after trying another browser, take a screenshot of the error and contact the helpdesk named in the notice. Include your application number if you have one, but do not send personal documents unless they ask you to through an official channel.
